name: Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)
description: World's largest health insurance scheme providing coverage up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation at empanelled hospitals across India.
eligibility: Families identified based on Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011. Includes deprived rural and occupational urban categories. No cap on family size or age.
documents: Aadhaar card (or any government-issued photo ID), Ration card, SECC list verification at Common Service Centre

name: Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana (MJPJAY)
description: Maharashtra's state health scheme that complements PM-JAY, offering cashless treatment up to ₹1.5 lakh (or ₹2.5 lakh for select major surgeries) at government and empanelled private hospitals for below-poverty-line families.
eligibility: Below Poverty Line (BPL) families, yellow and orange ration card holders, farmers with outstanding agricultural loans, and eligible occupational groups in Maharashtra.
documents: Yellow/orange ration card, Aadhaar card, income certificate, BPL certificate

name: Maharashtra Chief Minister's Medical Assistance Fund
description: Provides financial assistance for expensive medical treatment to patients who cannot afford treatment costs and are not covered under any other government scheme. Maximum assistance of ₹5 lakh per beneficiary.
eligibility: Maharashtra residents with annual family income below ₹8 lakh. Not covered under any other state or central health scheme. Serious illness requiring costly treatment.
documents: Income certificate from Tehsildar, Domicile certificate, Medical papers from treating hospital, Cost estimate from hospital, Aadhaar card, Bank account details

name: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
description: Conditional cash transfer scheme for promoting institutional delivery among poor pregnant women. Provides cash assistance to mothers delivering in government health facilities.
eligibility: All pregnant women belonging to BPL/SC/ST categories delivering in government hospitals. In Low Performing States, all women who deliver in government facilities are eligible.
documents: MCH card (Mother and Child Health card), Aadhaar card, Bank account passbook, BPL/SC/ST certificate

name: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK)
description: Free health screening and early intervention services for children from birth to 18 years. Covers 4Ds — Defects at birth, Diseases, Deficiencies, and Developmental delays including disabilities.
eligibility: All children from 0 to 18 years. Screening done at government schools, anganwadis, and government health facilities. Free treatment for detected conditions at District Early Intervention Centres (DEIC).
documents: Birth certificate or school ID, Aadhaar card of child/parent

name: National Mental Health Programme (NMHP)
description: Ensures availability and accessibility of mental health services for all, with emphasis on community-based mental health care. Provides free outpatient and inpatient care at District Mental Health Programme centres.
eligibility: All citizens. Priority to BPL families and persons with severe mental disorders.
documents: Government-issued ID, BPL card (for priority access), Referral slip from government health facility

name: Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS)
description: Comprehensive healthcare facility for Central Government employees, pensioners, and their dependents. Provides both OPD and IPD treatment at CGHS wellness centres and empanelled hospitals.
eligibility: Central Government employees (serving and retired), CGHS card holders and their registered dependents.
documents: CGHS card, Employee/pension ID, Aadhaar card

name: Mission Indradhanush
description: Universal immunization programme to improve vaccination coverage for children and pregnant women, targeting diseases like Diphtheria, Whooping Cough, Tetanus, Polio, Measles, Hepatitis B and Meningitis.
eligibility: Children up to 2 years of age and pregnant women. Special focus on unvaccinated and partially vaccinated populations in high-risk districts.
documents: Birth certificate or parent's ID for child registration. No documents required for vaccination — free and accessible at all government health centres.

name: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA)
description: Fixed-day antenatal care (ANC) services on 9th of every month at designated government health facilities. Provides free and comprehensive checkups for pregnant women in their 2nd and 3rd trimester.
eligibility: All pregnant women in their second and third trimester, particularly those who lack access to quality antenatal care.

name: Poshan Abhiyan (National Nutrition Mission)
description: Addresses malnutrition among children (0–6 years), pregnant women, and lactating mothers. Provides supplementary nutrition, growth monitoring, health check-ups, and referral services at Anganwadi centres.
eligibility: Children aged 0–6 years, pregnant women, lactating mothers, and adolescent girls.
documents: Aadhaar card or any government ID, MCH card for pregnant/lactating women, Birth certificate for children

name: Maharashtra Arogya Nidhi
description: Financial assistance for catastrophic illness treatment for patients below poverty line in Maharashtra who require treatment at state government hospitals for life-threatening diseases.
eligibility: Residents of Maharashtra below poverty line. Suffering from life-threatening or catastrophic illnesses. Admitted to government hospitals in Maharashtra.
documents: Yellow/orange ration card or BPL certificate, Medical papers, Cost estimate from superintendent of treating government hospital, Income proof, Domicile certificate

name: PM National Dialysis Programme
description: Free dialysis services for BPL patients suffering from chronic kidney disease at district hospitals across India. Aims to provide 2–3 sessions per week per patient.
eligibility: BPL patients with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) or End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD). Registered with district health authorities.
documents: BPL card, Aadhaar card, Medical certificate confirming CKD/ESRD from a registered medical practitioner, Referral from government hospital
